<!-- Generated by ModuleDocsGenerator from the annotations of org.hortonmachine.modules.DebrisVandre: do not edit, change the annotations and regenerate. -->

Traces the runout paths of debris flows from their trigger points, along the drainage directions, with the criteria of Burton and Bathurst: the debris moves on where the slope is at least 10 degrees and stops where it is under 4 degrees. In between, it travels at most the distance of the Vandre equation, 0.4 times the drop of the path above. The modified criteria move on from 8 degrees and have no lower limit.

**Toolbox folder:** Hydro-Geomorphology<br>
**Status:** Experimental<br>
**Keywords:** Debris flow, Runout, Vandre, Burton and Bathurst<br>
**Class:** `org.hortonmachine.modules.DebrisVandre`

**Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inElev` | raster file | m |  | The map of the elevation. |
| `inFlow` | raster file |  |  | The map of the drainage directions. |
| `inSlope` | raster file | ° |  | The map of the slope, in degrees. |
| `inTriggers` | raster file |  |  | The map of the trigger points: the cells with a value are triggers. |
| `inSoil` | raster file | m |  | The optional map of the soil depth, to cumulate the mobilized soil along the paths. |
| `inNet` | raster file |  |  | The optional map of the network, needed with the soil map. |
| `doWholenet` | boolean |  | `false` | With the soil map, propagate the cumulated soil down the whole network. |
| `pDistance` | double | m | `100.0` | With the soil map, the maximum distance of the paths. |
| `inObstacles` | vector file |  |  | An optional point map of obstacles on the network that stop the paths. |
| `pMode` | int |  | `0` | The criteria: 0 for Burton and Bathurst, 1 for the modified Burton and Bathurst. |

**Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outPaths` | output file |  | The vector of the runout paths, one for each trigger point. |
| `outIndexedTriggers` | output file |  | The vector of the trigger points, with the id of their path. |
| `outSoil` | output file |  | The optional map of the cumulated soil. |

**References**

- Vandre, B. C. (1985). Rudd Creek debris flow. In: Bowles, D. S. (Ed.), Delineation of landslide, flash flood and debris flow hazards in Utah. Utah Water Research Laboratory, Logan, 117-131.
- Burton, A., Bathurst, J. C. (1998). Physically based modelling of shallow landslide sediment yield at a catchment scale. Environmental Geology, 35(2-3), 89-99.
